title: Plans: which product, which heading, which role
blurb: Place planning information in the plan, project product description or work package description, and match planning actions to the right role.
question: Carrowford's race management company must set up the half marathon course before 6am on race day, with every marshal in high-visibility clothing. Which part of the work package description holds this, and who prepares the schedule for that work?

teach.h: Three planning products and the people behind them
teach.body: Formally, the plans practice facilitates communication and control by defining the products to be delivered and the means to deliver them: who, how, where, when and how much. Its key management products are the plan (project, stage, team and exception), the project product description and the work package description. In plain English: the timetable and budget, the description of what the whole project hands over, and the instruction sheet for one team's work. Practitioner items ask where a fact belongs and who should act.

teach.body: Written in starting up (in 'prepare the outline business case', with the PM consulting the senior user, senior supplier and executive), it describes the project's major products and their purpose, the user's quality expectations, the acceptance criteria and the acceptance methods. It works at project level and is used in closing to confirm acceptance. Detailed instructions for one team's work do not belong here; they go in the work package description.

teach.caption: These rows are the ones quoted in the official sample rationales; they are the safest anchors for role matching sets.

children.label: Business layer decides
children.sub: Set in the mandate or brief

teach.text: Two traps. A work package description carries scope, cost and time tolerances; putting a benefits or quality tolerance in a work package description is wrong. And the team manager, not the project manager, prepares the schedule for each work package.

teach.body: Kezia Oduya, the project manager, authorizes Paceline's race-day operations work package. The required course measurement method goes under techniques and procedures; the 6am start limit and high-visibility rule under constraints; the build-up stage plan under references; two days, £5,000 and two optional zones under tolerances. Lisa Ventnor, Paceline's race director and team manager, prepares the schedule for the work package. The executive sets the build-up stage tolerances and approves that stage plan.

items.label: plan types: project, stage, team, exception
where the PPD is written: prepare the outline business case

teach.h: Answering a planning product or role item
items: Ask the level: whole project (PPD, project plan), a stage (stage plan) or one team's work (WPD).
For a WPD fact: method is techniques, a limit is constraints, a higher plan is references.
For a role: business layer sets standards and project tolerances; executive sets stage tolerances.
PM decides stages and acts at work package tolerance; team manager schedules each work package.
WPD headings include techniques and procedures, constraints, references and tolerances (7.5).
WPD tolerances: scope, cost and time; not benefits or quality.
PPD: major products, user's quality expectations, acceptance criteria and methods; written in SU.
Business layer: planning standards and project tolerances. Executive: stage tolerances, approves stage plans (tab 7.1).
Team manager: schedules for each work package. Assurance: reviews progress against tolerances.

summary: You can now place planning facts in the plan, project product description or the right work package description heading. You can also match planning actions to the business layer, executive, senior user, project manager, team manager and project assurance.

A.q: Carrowford City Council is running its first half marathon. Project manager Kezia Oduya is writing the work package description for Paceline Events' course work. It states that the course must be measured using the method set by the national athletics body. Under which heading of the work package description should this be recorded?
A.why: Techniques and procedures state the requirements for how the work is to be done (7.5).

whyNot.0: Constraints are restrictions or limits on the work, such as permitted hours, safety or security measures.
whyNot.2: References point to applicable documents from higher-level plans.
whyNot.3: Tolerances set the permitted deviation in scope, cost and time.

A.q: Carrowford's race-day operations work package for Paceline Events states that no course set-up may start before 6am on race day and that every marshal must wear high-visibility clothing. Under which heading of the work package description should this be recorded?
A.why: Constraints are restrictions or limits on the work, such as authorized work hours and safety or security measures (7.5).

whyNot.0: References list documents from higher-level plans that apply to the work.
whyNot.1: Tolerances set the permitted deviation in scope, cost and time.
whyNot.2: Techniques and procedures say how the work is to be done, not the limits placed on it.

A.q: Carrowford City Council has run only small events before and has no planning standards for something of this size. Kezia Oduya asks who should supply the planning standards the council requires for the half marathon. Which role should do this?
A.why: The business layer provides the planning standards required by the business (tab 7.1).

whyNot.0: The executive sets stage tolerances and approves stage plans, but planning standards come from the business layer.
whyNot.1: Project support can help compile plans, but it does not set the business's planning standards.
whyNot.3: The project manager uses the planning standards to prepare plans.

B.q: Carrowford's half marathon is about to enter its build-up stage. Kezia Oduya has prepared the stage plan and needs someone to set the stage's time and cost tolerances and approve the plan. Which role should do this?
B.why: The executive defines the tolerances for each stage and approves stage plans (tab 7.1).

whyNot.0: The business layer sets project tolerances, documented in the mandate or confirmed for the brief.
whyNot.2: Project assurance reviews progress against agreed tolerances; it does not set them.
whyNot.3: The project manager sets work package tolerances, not stage tolerances.

B.q: Lisa Ventnor, race director at Paceline Events, leads the team for Carrowford's race-day operations work package. Kezia Oduya, the project manager, has authorized the work package. Who should prepare the schedule for this work package?
B.why: The team manager prepares schedules for each work package (tab 7.1). Lisa leads the team, so she is the team manager.

whyNot.0: The PM prepares project and stage plans and work package descriptions, but the work package schedule is the team manager's.
whyNot.1: The senior supplier commits supplier resources at board level; it does not schedule a work package.
whyNot.3: Project support may assist with planning tools, but it does not own the work package schedule.

B.q: In starting up the Carrowford Half Marathon, Kezia Oduya records that the council will accept the event only if the course is certified before entries open, the safety advisory group approves the safety plan eight weeks before race day, and refill stations replace single-use bottles. Where should she record these?
options: The product description for the course
B.why: Acceptance criteria for the project's major products are part of the project product description, written in starting up (7.5).

whyNot.1: The initiation stage plan schedules initiation work; it does not define acceptance criteria.
whyNot.2: A work package description instructs one team; project acceptance criteria sit at project level.
whyNot.3: A product description holds one product's specification; project-wide acceptance criteria belong in the PPD.

C.q: Carrowford's half marathon is in its build-up stage. Kezia Oduya's work package description for the volunteer training work includes time, cost and scope tolerances, plus a benefits tolerance of 10% on the number of first-time runners. Is this an appropriate application of the 'plans' practice, and why?
options: Yes, because tolerances can be set for seven aspects at plan levels
Yes, because the project manager sets work package tolerances
No, because the team manager sets work package tolerances
No, because a work package carries scope, cost and time tolerances
C.why: Work package descriptions carry targets and tolerances for scope, cost and time; benefits and quality tolerances are not agreed in a WPD (7.5, 11.2.1).

whyNot.0: Plans can carry tolerances for several aspects, but a work package description does not hold a benefits tolerance.
whyNot.1: It is true that the PM sets work package tolerances, but that does not make a benefits tolerance appropriate here.
whyNot.2: The PM sets work package tolerances; the team manager sets tolerances for team members.

C.q: During Carrowford's build-up stage, the marketing work package is forecast to finish four days late, beyond its two-day tolerance but well within the stage tolerance. Kezia Oduya instructs the team manager to add a second designer for a week to recover the time. Is this an appropriate application of the 'plans' practice, and why?
options: Yes, because the PM instructs corrective action at work package level
Yes, because project assurance reviews progress against tolerances
No, because the executive must approve changes to work packages
No, because a forecast breach needs an exception report to the board
C.why: The project manager instructs corrective action when work-package-level tolerances are forecast to be exceeded; the stage stays within tolerance, so no board decision is needed (tab 7.1).

whyNot.1: It is true that assurance reviews progress against tolerances, but that does not explain the PM's action.
whyNot.2: Within stage tolerance, corrective action on a work package is for the PM, not the executive.
whyNot.3: Exception reports are for forecast breaches of stage or project tolerance, not work package tolerance.

C.q: Carrowford's draft build-up stage plan is being reviewed. The senior user asks Kezia Oduya to add time for volunteer briefings and for the council events team, who will run future races, to shadow Paceline on race week. Is this an appropriate application of the 'plans' practice, and why?
options: Yes, because the senior user keeps plans consistent with the user view
Yes, because the senior user specifies the benefits of the event
No, because the project manager is the person who prepares stage plans
No, because the executive approves stage plans and sets their tolerances
C.why: The senior user should ensure that project and stage plans remain consistent with the user perspective (tab 7.1).

whyNot.1: It is true that the senior user specifies benefits, but that does not explain reviewing the plan for user needs.
whyNot.2: It is true that the PM prepares stage plans, but the senior user still checks them against the user perspective.
whyNot.3: It is true that the executive approves stage plans, but that does not stop the senior user influencing their content.

reteach.title: Zoom levels: project, stage, team
reteach.question: If planning were a map, which product shows the whole country, which a city, and which one street?

blocks.body: The project product description and project plan show the whole country: the major products, how the project will be judged acceptable, and the high-level route. A stage plan shows the city: detailed work for the current stage. A work package description shows one street: exactly how one team will produce its products, within what limits, using which references, and with scope, cost and time tolerances.

blocks.text: Detail drifts down, not up: method and limits for one team's work go in its work package description, not in the project product description.

explain.body: A plan sets out what, where, when, how and who for the project or part of it, including the work to be performed. The project product description, written in starting up, describes the major products, the user's quality expectations, acceptance criteria and acceptance methods.

test.q: Carrowford's project manager needs a product that shows the build-up stage's work breakdown structure and the work package descriptions for that stage. Which product holds this as its 'work to be performed'?
test.why: A plan's 'work to be performed' shows the work in the plan's scope as a WBS with the associated work package descriptions (7.5).

whyNot.0: The PPD defines the major products and acceptance, not the work breakdown.
whyNot.1: The project brief is the foundation for initiation.
whyNot.3: The communication approach covers stakeholder communication.

explain.body: It passes responsibility for work formally to a team manager and holds what they need: techniques and procedures, constraints, references and targets and tolerances for scope, cost and time.

test.q: Carrowford's work package description for volunteer training lists the build-up stage plan and the event safety plan as documents the team must follow. Under which heading does this belong?
test.why: References list applicable documents from higher-level plans (7.5).

whyNot.0: Constraints are limits such as hours or safety rules.
whyNot.1: Tolerances are permitted deviations in scope, cost and time.
whyNot.2: Techniques and procedures describe how the work is done.

explain.body: The business layer sets project tolerances in the mandate or confirms them for the brief. The executive defines stage tolerances and approves stage plans. The PM sets work package tolerances and instructs corrective action when they are forecast to be exceeded.

test.q: Carrowford's cabinet has capped the council's net contribution to the half marathon at £300,000. Which role should set this as a project tolerance?
test.why: The business layer sets project tolerances, documented in the project mandate or confirmed for the project brief (tab 7.1).

whyNot.1: The PM sets work package tolerances.

explain.body: The senior user keeps project and stage plans consistent with the user perspective. The team manager prepares schedules for each work package. Project assurance reviews stage and project progress against agreed tolerances.

test.q: Carrowford's internal audit team has been appointed to provide assurance to the board. Which planning activity fits this role?
test.why: Project assurance reviews stage and project progress against agreed tolerances (tab 7.1).

whyNot.1: Setting stage tolerances is the executive's role.
whyNot.2: Work package schedules are prepared by team managers.
whyNot.3: Planning standards come from the business layer.
